## formal
Under Hypothesis (S), with the ten Majorana generators $\gamma_{1}, \dots, \gamma_{10}$ of the five modes ($\gamma_{p}^{2} = 1$), the creation operators $v_{j} = \tfrac12(\gamma_{2j-1} + I\gamma_{2j})$, the occupation numbers $N_{j} = v_{j}v_{j}^{*}$ ($v_{j}^{*}v_{j} = 1 - N_{j}$ is the hole number), $N = \sum_{j}N_{j}$, the chirality $\Gamma = (-1)^{N} = \prod_{j}(1 - 2N_{j})$ (the parity of the total mode number), the sixteen components of one generation the even part $V_{+}$ of $V = \Lambda^{\bullet}\C^{5}$, which contains the empty state, and the Majorana element $T = v_{1}v_{2}v_{3}v_{4}v_{5}$ of \claimref{standard-model.majorana-element}; $I$ is the commuting unit of the module (the field theory's unit in the store's reading).
\begin{enumerate}
\item \emph{(The Klein twist carries no charge.)} For an even involution $k$ commuting with $I$, the twist $V_{k} = (1 + Ik)(1 + I)^{-1}$ of \claimref{synthesis.wedge-reflections-compose-to-the-two-pi-rotor-so-geometric-modular-conjugations-give-interacting-spin-statistics}(iv) is $p_{+} - Ip_{-}$ with $p_{\pm} = \tfrac12(1 \pm k)$: a polynomial in $k$. So it exists on every graded module, whatever the number of components; it commutes with everything that commutes with $k$, in particular with every even element; every map that preserves the grading preserves it; and on an odd element $a$, $V_{k}aV_{k}^{-1} = -Iak$, which for two or more modes is not a multiple of $a$ nor in the span of the generators over $\mathrm{span}\{1, I\}$ (for one mode $-Iak$ is again a generator, and the twist is a quarter turn of that mode). Proved: it is an order-four element with $V_{k}^{2} = k$, a polynomial in the grading, present for every content, and for two or more modes it assigns no charge to the generators. Argued, as a reading of these facts: no condition on the content can come from it.
\item \emph{(The pseudoscalar of the ten.)} $\omega = \gamma_{1}\gamma_{2}\cdots\gamma_{10}$ satisfies $\omega^{2} = -1$, anticommutes with every $\gamma_{p}$ and commutes with all $45$ bivectors $\gamma_{p}\gamma_{q}$, hence with the gauge algebra of every stage of the chain; and, for the orientation $\gamma_{1}\cdots\gamma_{10}$ and the stored conventions ($v_{j}$ creation operators), $\omega = -I\,(-1)^{N} = -I\,\Gamma$. So $\omega$ acts on all sixteen components of $V_{+}$ by the same unit $-I$ (and by $+I$ on the conjugate sixteen $V_{-}$), with one odd charge on every component, on fifteen components as on sixteen. Precisely: conjugation by $\omega$ is the grading automorphism of the Clifford algebra, of order two; the order-four action is the action on the module $V$, where $\omega^{2} = -1$ is the parity of one-fermion states. With $X = 5(B - L) - 4Y = 5 - 2N$, $\omega = \exp(-\tfrac{\pi}{2}IX)$: $\omega$ generates the centre of $\Spin(10)$ and is the $\Z_{4}$ inside $U(1)_{X}$ of the literature. This identification is classical, not new; what is recorded here is its form in the stored five-mode algebra. It is the product of the five mode rotors, $\omega = \prod_{j}\exp(\tfrac{\pi}{2}\gamma_{2j-1}\gamma_{2j})$, each generated by a bivector that preserves the split into slot and pair generators, so $\omega$ lies in the group generated by the Pati-Salam algebra (and by $\uu(5)$ and $\so(10)$).
\item \emph{(The Majorana element is odd under it.)} $T$ has grade five and $\omega T\omega^{-1} = -T$; on $V_{+}$ the bilinear form $B(\psi, T\varphi)$ of the cited claim changes sign under $\psi, \varphi \mapsto \omega\psi, \omega\varphi$. The parity of $T$ under $\omega$ is the reduction modulo $4$ of its charge under $X$: $[B - L, T] = -2T$ and $[Y, T] = 0$ give charge $-10 \equiv 2$. Every mass form on the sixteen, of grade $1$, $3$ or $5$, anticommutes with $\omega$, Dirac terms included: the sign change is not special to $T$. What separates $T$ is compensation by the gauge group. Let $z = \exp(\tfrac{\pi}{2}(\gamma_{1}\gamma_{2} - \gamma_{3}\gamma_{4}))$, the element $-1$ of $\su(2)_{L}$ on the slot doublet (modes $1, 2$ the slot modes); $\omega z$, and likewise $\omega\exp(-2\pi IY)$, which differs from it by a central element of $\su(3)$, lies in $\omega$ times the Standard Model group and fixes the four slot vectors, so a Dirac term of grade one keeps $\omega$ modulo the Standard Model group; $T$ is invariant under that group, so nothing compensates, $\omega$ is not in the group generated by the subalgebra that fixes $T$ (the Standard Model algebra $\su(3) \oplus \su(2)_{L} \oplus \uu(1)_{Y}$ of clause (2) of the cited claim), and a vev along $T$ breaks $\omega$, and every element of $\omega$ times the Standard Model group, to $\omega^{2} = -1$. Proved: $\omega$ is in the Pati-Salam group and is odd on $T$, with no compensation. Argued, as a reading: in the stored chain there is no stage at which $\omega$, taken modulo the gauge group of the stage, is both unbroken and not a gauge transformation, once the Majorana term is present; without the Majorana term, $\omega$ modulo the Standard Model group is unbroken and is not a gauge transformation of the Standard Model stage.
\item \emph{(Arithmetic of signed counts; no anomaly statement is made.)} An order-four element with square $-1$ that commutes with the Standard Model algebra acts on each of the six multiplets of $V_{+}$, of dimensions $6, 3, 3, 2, 1, 1$, by $\pm I$. The difference between the numbers of components with $+I$ and with $-I$ is $-16$ for $\omega$ and $0$ for $\omega z$ (eight doublet against eight singlet components; the two differ by a gauge element), and takes the values $\pm 16$ and $0$ among others; on fifteen components (the neutral singlet removed) it is odd for every choice, so for an odd number of fifteen-component generations it is never divisible by $2$, and with the same uniform choice in each generation it is $15n_{g}$, divisible by $16$ only when $16$ divides $n_{g}$.
\end{enumerate}
Clause (4) is what a statement of the form "the difference must vanish modulo $16$" would give; that statement is literature cited from memory in the open problem and is neither imported nor derived here.

## technical
The open problem asks whether the store has an order-four symmetry whose square is the grading, and whether it could force sixteen components per generation. Two candidates are in the store and they behave differently. The Klein twist, which enters the geometric modular conjugations, is $p_{+} - Ip_{-}$: the identity on the even part and the unit on the odd part. It is built from the grading alone, so every theory with a grading has it, with one component or with sixteen, and conjugation by it sends a generator $a$ to $-Iak$, a product with the full parity operator. It is not a transformation of the generators by a phase, and nothing about the content can be read from it.

The element that acts by one phase on all sixteen components is the pseudoscalar of the ten Majorana generators. Its square is $-1$, it commutes with every bivector, so with every gauge algebra of the chain, and it equals minus the unit times the chirality, so it is $-I$ on the sixteen. It generates the centre of the rotor group of the ten (the classical centre of $\Spin(10)$, the quarter turn of the charge $X = 5(B - L) - 4Y$), a product of five quarter-period mode rotors, each inside the Pati-Salam algebra: at the Pati-Salam stage and above it is a gauge transformation, and the sixteenth component is already forced there by the multiplet structure. Below that stage the chain is broken by the element $T$, the product of the five creation operators, which is the Majorana term of the neutral singlet. $T$ has odd grade, so the pseudoscalar anticommutes with it; but so does every mass form, the Dirac forms included, since all have odd grade. The difference is that a Dirac form of grade one is a doublet of $\su(2)_{L}$, so the pseudoscalar times the centre of that group fixes it, while $T$ is invariant under the whole Standard Model group and nothing can undo its sign. So Dirac terms keep the order-four element modulo the Standard Model group, and the element that gives the singlet its Majorana mass breaks it to its square. Read against the chain (argued): without the Majorana term the class of the pseudoscalar modulo the Standard Model group is an unbroken symmetry that is not a gauge transformation; with it, against the stored premise that the term is realised, no such symmetry is left. The same structure appears in the companion result on mass terms as pair terms of the arrays, where the two charges that separate Majorana from Dirac terms are those of the pseudoscalar and of the pseudoscalar times the centre of $\su(2)_{L}$. The last clause records the counting that the literature's modulo-16 statement would use, as arithmetic: fifteen components always give an odd signed count.

## lay
Some consistency arguments in particle physics use a symmetry that returns to the starting point only after four steps, and whose second step is the sign flip of all fermions; such a symmetry can require the fermions of one generation to come in sixteens. The store was thought to contain a symmetry of this kind in a twist used for its vacuum states. This result shows that the twist is built from the sign flip alone and so says nothing about how many fermions there are. A second four-step element does treat all sixteen fermions alike, but in the series' chain of symmetry breaking it is either part of the gauge symmetry, or (argued) it is broken by the very term that makes the sixteenth fermion, the heavy neutrino partner, massive. So within the stored chain it cannot be used to argue for sixteen rather than fifteen, unless that mass term is absent.

## one-liner
Under Hypothesis (S), the Klein twist is $p_{+} - Ip_{-}$, a polynomial in the grading that assigns no charge to generators; the pseudoscalar $\omega$ of the ten Majoranas has $\omega^{2} = -1$, equals $-I(-1)^{N}$ ($-I$ on all sixteen; the classical centre of $\Spin(10)$), lies in the Pati-Salam group, and reverses every mass form; Dirac terms keep it modulo the Standard Model group, while the Majorana element $T$ is invariant under that group, so a vev along $T$ breaks it to the grading.

proofs.proof-main.tex:
\emph{(1).} Since $k^{2} = 1$ and $I^{2} = -1$ commute, $(1 + I)^{-1} = \tfrac12(1 - I)$ and $(1 + Ik)(1 - I) = 1 + k - I(1 - k)$, so $V_{k} = p_{+} - Ip_{-}$; this is the element of \claimref{synthesis.wedge-reflections-compose-to-the-two-pi-rotor-so-geometric-modular-conjugations-give-interacting-spin-statistics}(iv), where $V_{k}^{2} = k$ is proved. Being a polynomial in $k$ with coefficients in $\mathrm{span}\{1, I\}$, it is defined whenever $k$ is, commutes with whatever commutes with $k$ and $I$, and is carried to itself by every map that fixes $k$ and $I$. For odd $a$, $p_{\pm}a = ap_{\mp}$, so $V_{k}aV_{k}^{-1} = (p_{+} - Ip_{-})a(p_{+} + Ip_{-}) = I(p_{+}ap_{-} - p_{-}ap_{+}) = Ia(p_{-} - p_{+}) = -Iak$. For two modes with generators $e_{1}, \dots, e_{4}$ and $k = e_{1}e_{2}e_{3}e_{4}$, $-Ie_{1}k = -Ie_{2}e_{3}e_{4}$, a product of three generators, not a combination of generators (checked in $\Cl(4,1)$, where the pseudoscalar is a central unit: the result has grade two, while $ce_{j}$ and $cIe_{j}$ have grades one and four). With more modes $k$ contains more factors. For one mode with generators $e_{1}, e_{2}$, $k$ is $I e_{1}e_{2}$ up to sign and $-Ie_{1}k = \pm e_{2}$, a generator: there the twist is the quarter turn of the mode.

\emph{(2).} $\omega^{2} = (-1)^{10\cdot 9/2} = -1$. Moving $\gamma_{p}$ through $\omega$ passes nine other generators, so $\omega\gamma_{p} = -\gamma_{p}\omega$, and $\omega$ commutes with products of two generators. From $N_{j} = v_{j}v_{j}^{*} = \tfrac12(1 - I\gamma_{2j-1}\gamma_{2j})$, $\gamma_{2j-1}\gamma_{2j} = -I(1 - 2N_{j})$, so $\omega = (-I)^{5}\prod_{j}(1 - 2N_{j}) = -I(-1)^{N}$. On $V_{+}$, which contains the empty state ($N = 0$; the projector $\prod_{j}v_{j}^{*}v_{j}$ is annihilated by every $v_{j}^{*}$, and $\omega$ times it is $-I$ times it), $\Gamma = 1$ and $\omega = -I$; on $V_{-}$, $\omega = +I$. Since $\omega\gamma_{p}\omega^{-1} = -\gamma_{p}$, conjugation by $\omega$ is the grading automorphism, of order two, while on $V$ the element itself has order four. On a state of mode number $N$, $\exp(-\tfrac{\pi}{2}I(5 - 2N)) = (-I)^{5}(-1)^{N} = -I(-1)^{N}$, so $\omega = \exp(-\tfrac{\pi}{2}IX)$ with $X = 5 - 2N$; with $n$ and $k$ the slot and pair occupations, $Y = (3n - 2k)/6$ and $B - L = 1 - 2k/3$, so $5(B - L) - 4Y = 5 - 2n - 2k = X$. The rotors of the ten are generated by the $45$ bivectors, $\omega$ commutes with all of them, and $\omega^{2} = -1$ is the other central element: $\omega$ generates the centre, of order four (classical). Since $(\gamma_{2j-1}\gamma_{2j})^{2} = -1$, $\exp(\tfrac{\pi}{2}\gamma_{2j-1}\gamma_{2j}) = \gamma_{2j-1}\gamma_{2j}$, and the two generators of one mode are both slot generators or both pair generators, so each of these bivectors is among the $21$ of Proposition \claimref{standard-model.automorphisms-preserve-slot-pair-split-are}. The statement about fifteen components: removing one component of $V_{+}$ does not change the action on the others.

\emph{(3).} $T$ is a product of five elements each linear in the generators, and the five pairs are disjoint, so $T$ is of grade five (\claimref{standard-model.majorana-element}); $\omega$ anticommutes with every element of odd grade by (2), so $\omega T\omega^{-1} = -T$. On $V_{+}$, $\omega = -I$ and $B$ is bilinear over $\mathrm{span}\{1, I\}$, so $B(\omega\psi, T\omega\varphi) = I^{2}B(\psi, T\varphi) = -B(\psi, T\varphi)$; the same computation applies to every bilinear form in two fields of the sixteen, and in the algebra every mass form has grade $1$, $3$ or $5$ and anticommutes with $\omega$. The element $z = \exp(\tfrac{\pi}{2}(\gamma_{1}\gamma_{2} - \gamma_{3}\gamma_{4})) = -\gamma_{1}\gamma_{2}\gamma_{3}\gamma_{4}$ is generated by a difference of slot mode bivectors, which commutes with $T$ and lies in $\su(2)_{L}$; it anticommutes with the four slot generators and commutes with the six pair generators and with $T$. So $\omega z$ commutes with the slot generators and $(\omega z)T(\omega z)^{-1} = -T$. On states $\exp(-2\pi IY) = (-1)^{n}\exp(\tfrac{2\pi}{3}Ik)$, which is $z$ times a central element of $\su(3)$. Every element of the group generated by the subalgebra fixing $T$ commutes with $T$; $\omega$ does not, so it is not in that group; that subalgebra is the Standard Model algebra, and a vev along $T$ breaks Pati-Salam to it, by clauses (2) and (3) of the cited claim. The bit of the neutral singlet is fixed at the stages that leave $\uu(5)$ (\claimref{synthesis.neutral-singlet-bit-decided-by-gauge-algebra-leaving-u5}), which is where $\omega$ is a gauge transformation.

\emph{(4).} The six multiplets of $V_{+}$ under the Standard Model algebra are pairwise inequivalent, so an element commuting with the algebra is a scalar of $\mathrm{span}\{1, I\}$ on each, and with square $-1$ the scalar is $\pm I$. The signed sums $\pm 6 \pm 3 \pm 3 \pm 2 \pm 1 \pm 1$ include $16$, $-16$ and $0$ (for instance $6 + 2 - 3 - 3 - 1 - 1$, the doublets against the singlets, which is $\omega z$ up to an overall sign). The sum of $6, 3, 3, 2, 1$ is $15$, odd, and changing a sign changes a signed sum by an even number, so every signed sum for fifteen components is odd; a sum of an odd number of odd integers is odd. $15n_{g} \equiv -n_{g} \pmod{16}$.

check_py:
"""synthesis.order-four-elements-with-square-the-grading-and-the-majorana-element: exact checks.

Two order-four elements whose square is a grading occur in the store. (a) The Klein twist
V = (1 + I k)(1 + I)^{-1} of an even involution k (the grading) with the unit I: checked in Cl(4,1), where
e_1 .. e_4 are the Majorana generators of two modes, the pseudoscalar I is central with I^2 = -1, and
k = e_1e_2e_3e_4. (b) The pseudoscalar omega of the ten Majorana generators of the five modes, in Cl(10,0);
elements of the complexified algebra are pairs (A, B) for A + I B with I a commuting unit. Checks:
  (1) V = p_+ - I p_-, V^2 = k, V commutes with every even element, and Ad_V(e_1) = -I e_1 k is not in the span
      of the generators over span{1, I}: the twist assigns no charge to a generator;
  (2) omega^2 = -1, omega anticommutes with the ten generators and commutes with the 45 bivectors; it is the
      product of the five mode rotors exp((pi/2) e_{2j-1}e_{2j}) = e_{2j-1}e_{2j};
  (3) with N_j = v_j v_j^* the occupation numbers (v_j creation operators), omega = -I (-1)^N; on the projector of
      the empty state, which the v_j^* annihilate, omega is -I: the unit -I on the sixteen, +I on its conjugate;
  (4) the Majorana element T = v_1 v_2 v_3 v_4 v_5 is of grade five and omega T omega^{-1} = -T; with z the centre
      of su(2)_L (modes 1, 2 the slot modes), omega z commutes with the four slot generators and still reverses T;
  (5) signed sums of the multiplet dimensions (6, 3, 3, 2, 1, 1) and (6, 3, 3, 2, 1).
"""
from fractions import Fraction as F
import GA
from tp_premise import premise

MODES = 5
GENS = 2 * MODES
SQ10 = GA.sig(GENS, 0)
SIXTEEN = (6, 3, 3, 2, 1, 1)      # (2,3), (1,3bar), (1,3bar), (2,1), (1,1), (1,1): the sixteen of one generation
FIFTEEN = (6, 3, 3, 2, 1)         # without the neutral singlet
MODULUS = 16


def check_klein_twist_is_a_polynomial_in_the_grading():
    premise("synthesis.wedge-reflections-compose-to-the-two-pi-rotor-so-geometric-modular-conjugations-give-interacting-spin-statistics")
    sq = GA.sig(4, 1)
    e = [GA.gen(i) for i in range(5)]
    one = GA.sc(F(1))

    def prod(*xs):
        out = one
        for x in xs:
            out = GA.mul(out, x, sq)
        return out

    I = prod(*e)                                                # central pseudoscalar of Cl(4,1)
    k = prod(e[0], e[1], e[2], e[3])                            # the grading of the two-mode algebra
    assert GA.eq(prod(I, I), GA.neg(one)) and GA.eq(prod(k, k), one)
    for g in e:
        assert GA.commutes(I, g, sq)
    for g in e[:4]:
        assert GA.anticommutes(k, g, sq)                        # generators are odd
    half = F(1, 2)
    V = GA.scal(half, prod(GA.add(one, prod(I, k)), GA.sub(one, I)))        # (1 + I k)(1 + I)^{-1}
    Vinv = GA.scal(half, prod(GA.sub(one, prod(I, k)), GA.add(one, I)))
    p_plus = GA.scal(half, GA.add(one, k))
    p_minus = GA.scal(half, GA.sub(one, k))
    assert GA.eq(prod(V, Vinv), one)
    assert GA.eq(V, GA.sub(p_plus, prod(I, p_minus)))           # V = p_+ - I p_-: a polynomial in k
    assert GA.eq(prod(V, V), k)                                 # order four, square the grading
    for a in range(4):
        for b in range(a + 1, 4):
            assert GA.commutes(V, prod(e[a], e[b]), sq)         # commutes with every even element
    ad = prod(V, e[0], Vinv)
    assert GA.eq(ad, GA.neg(prod(I, e[0], k)))                  # Ad_V(e_1) = -I e_1 k
    grades = set(len(b) for b, c in ad.items() if c != 0)
    assert grades == {2}                                        # e_1 e_5 up to sign: not c e_j or c I e_j (grades 1, 4)
    assert GA.eq(prod(V, V, e[0], Vinv, Vinv), GA.neg(e[0]))    # Ad_V^2 is the grading automorphism
    return True


def blade(*idx):
    out = GA.sc(F(1))
    for i in idx:
        out = GA.mul(out, GA.gen(i), SQ10)
    return out


def check_pseudoscalar_of_the_ten_generators():
    premise("standard-model.automorphisms-preserve-slot-pair-split-are")
    omega = blade(*range(GENS))
    one = GA.sc(F(1))
    assert GA.eq(GA.mul(omega, omega, SQ10), GA.neg(one))       # omega^2 = -1
    for p in range(GENS):
        assert GA.anticommutes(omega, GA.gen(p), SQ10)
    count = 0
    for p in range(GENS):
        for q in range(p + 1, GENS):
            assert GA.commutes(omega, blade(p, q), SQ10)
            count += 1
    assert count == 45
    # omega is the product of the five mode rotors: (e_a e_b)^2 = -1, so exp((pi/2) e_a e_b) = e_a e_b
    rot = one
    for j in range(MODES):
        r = blade(2 * j, 2 * j + 1)
        assert GA.eq(GA.mul(r, r, SQ10), GA.neg(one))
        rot = GA.mul(rot, r, SQ10)
    assert GA.eq(rot, omega)
    return True


def cmul(x, y):
    """(A + I B)(C + I D) with I a commuting unit, I^2 = -1."""
    A, B = x
    C, D = y
    return (GA.sub(GA.mul(A, C, SQ10), GA.mul(B, D, SQ10)), GA.add(GA.mul(A, D, SQ10), GA.mul(B, C, SQ10)))


ZERO = GA.sc(F(0))


def mode_ops(j):
    half = F(1, 2)
    a, b = GA.gen(2 * j), GA.gen(2 * j + 1)
    v = (GA.scal(half, a), GA.scal(half, b))                    # v_j = (e_a + I e_b)/2
    vd = (GA.scal(half, a), GA.scal(-half, b))                  # its adjoint (e_a - I e_b)/2
    return v, vd


def ceq(x, y):
    return GA.eq(x[0], y[0]) and GA.eq(x[1], y[1])


def times_unit(x, sign):
    """(sign I) x for sign = 1 or -1."""
    return (GA.scal(F(-sign), x[1]), GA.scal(F(sign), x[0]))


def check_pseudoscalar_is_the_unit_times_the_chirality():
    premise("standard-model.majorana-element")
    one = (GA.sc(F(1)), ZERO)
    omega = (blade(*range(GENS)), ZERO)
    parity = one                                                # (-1)^N, N the total occupation number
    empty = one                                                 # projector of the empty state: all holes
    for j in range(MODES):
        v, vd = mode_ops(j)
        occ = cmul(v, vd)                                       # N_j = v_j v_j^*, v_j the creation operator
        hole = cmul(vd, v)
        assert ceq(cmul(occ, occ), occ) and ceq((GA.add(occ[0], hole[0]), GA.add(occ[1], hole[1])), one)
        parity = cmul(parity, (GA.sub(one[0], GA.scal(F(2), occ[0])), GA.neg(GA.scal(F(2), occ[1]))))
        empty = cmul(empty, hole)
    assert ceq(cmul(parity, parity), one)
    assert ceq(omega, times_unit(parity, -1))                   # omega = -I (-1)^N
    assert not ceq(omega, times_unit(parity, 1))
    # the empty state: annihilated by every v_j^*, even, and omega acts on it by -I
    assert not GA.is_zero(empty[0]) and ceq(cmul(empty, empty), empty)
    for j in range(MODES):
        gone = cmul(mode_ops(j)[1], empty)
        assert GA.is_zero(gone[0]) and GA.is_zero(gone[1])
        made = cmul(mode_ops(j)[0], empty)
        assert not (GA.is_zero(made[0]) and GA.is_zero(made[1]))
    assert ceq(cmul(parity, empty), empty)                      # N = 0: in the even part, the sixteen
    assert ceq(cmul(omega, empty), times_unit(empty, -1))       # omega = -I on the empty state
    # one creation operator moves to the odd part, where omega = +I
    odd_state = cmul(mode_ops(MODES - 1)[0], empty)
    assert ceq(cmul(omega, odd_state), times_unit(odd_state, 1))
    return True


def check_majorana_element_is_odd_under_the_pseudoscalar():
    premise("standard-model.majorana-element")
    premise("synthesis.neutral-singlet-bit-decided-by-gauge-algebra-leaving-u5")
    T = (GA.sc(F(1)), ZERO)
    for j in range(MODES):
        T = cmul(T, mode_ops(j)[0])
    omega = blade(*range(GENS))
    omega_inv = GA.neg(omega)
    for part in T:
        assert not GA.is_zero(part)
        assert set(len(b) for b, c in part.items() if c != 0) == {MODES}      # grade five
        conj = GA.mul(GA.mul(omega, part, SQ10), omega_inv, SQ10)
        assert GA.eq(conj, GA.neg(part))                        # omega T omega^{-1} = -T
    # the mode bivectors: [sum_j e_{2j-1}e_{2j}, T] = c I T with c = 2 * MODES up to the sign convention of v_j,
    # so T has charge 2 under each mode rotor, and every difference of two mode bivectors commutes with T
    def comm(X, part):
        return GA.sub(GA.mul(X, part, SQ10), GA.mul(part, X, SQ10))
    mode_biv = [GA.mul(GA.gen(2 * j), GA.gen(2 * j + 1), SQ10) for j in range(MODES)]
    total = GA.add(*mode_biv)
    i_T = (GA.neg(T[1]), T[0])                                   # I T
    c_re, c_im = comm(total, T[0]), comm(total, T[1])
    weight = 2 * MODES
    plus = GA.eq(c_re, GA.scal(F(weight), i_T[0])) and GA.eq(c_im, GA.scal(F(weight), i_T[1]))
    minus = GA.eq(c_re, GA.scal(F(-weight), i_T[0])) and GA.eq(c_im, GA.scal(F(-weight), i_T[1]))
    assert plus or minus
    for j in range(MODES):
        for l in range(j + 1, MODES):
            d = GA.sub(mode_biv[j], mode_biv[l])
            assert GA.is_zero(comm(d, T[0])) and GA.is_zero(comm(d, T[1]))
    return True


SLOT_MODES = (0, 1)        # the two slot modes (four slot generators); the other three are pair modes


def check_dirac_terms_keep_the_pseudoscalar_modulo_the_gauge_group():
    premise("standard-model.majorana-element")
    premise("standard-model.automorphisms-preserve-slot-pair-split-are")
    one = GA.sc(F(1))
    omega = blade(*range(GENS))
    T = (one, ZERO)
    for j in range(MODES):
        T = cmul(T, mode_ops(j)[0])
    b0 = blade(2 * SLOT_MODES[0], 2 * SLOT_MODES[0] + 1)
    b1 = blade(2 * SLOT_MODES[1], 2 * SLOT_MODES[1] + 1)
    # z = exp((pi/2)(b0 - b1)) = b0 (-b1): generated by a difference of slot mode bivectors (the T_3 direction
    # of su(2)_L), the element -1 of that group on a slot doublet
    z = GA.neg(GA.mul(b0, b1, SQ10))
    assert GA.eq(GA.mul(z, z, SQ10), one)
    slot_gens = [GA.gen(2 * j + i) for j in SLOT_MODES for i in (0, 1)]
    pair_gens = [GA.gen(p) for p in range(GENS) if p >= 2 * len(SLOT_MODES)]
    assert len(slot_gens) == 4 and len(pair_gens) == 6
    for g in slot_gens:
        assert GA.anticommutes(z, g, SQ10)                      # -1 on the slot doublet
    for g in pair_gens:
        assert GA.commutes(z, g, SQ10)
    for part in T:
        assert GA.is_zero(GA.sub(GA.mul(z, part, SQ10), GA.mul(part, z, SQ10)))     # T is invariant under z
    oz = GA.mul(omega, z, SQ10)
    oz_inv = GA.mul(z, GA.neg(omega), SQ10)
    assert GA.eq(GA.mul(oz, oz_inv, SQ10), one)
    for g in slot_gens:
        assert GA.commutes(oz, g, SQ10)                         # omega z fixes the grade-one (slot) mass forms
        assert GA.anticommutes(omega, g, SQ10)                  # which omega alone reverses
    for part in T:
        assert GA.eq(GA.mul(GA.mul(oz, part, SQ10), oz_inv, SQ10), GA.neg(part))    # and still reverses T
    # every odd blade anticommutes with omega: grades one, three and five
    for idx in ((0,), (0, 4, 5), (1, 2, 6), (0, 2, 4, 6, 8), (1, 3, 5, 7, 9)):
        assert GA.anticommutes(omega, blade(*idx), SQ10)
    return True


def signed_sums(dims):
    out = []
    for mask in range(2 ** len(dims)):
        out.append(sum(d if (mask >> i) & 1 else -d for i, d in enumerate(dims)))
    return out


def check_signed_dimension_sums_for_fifteen_and_sixteen():
    premise("standard-model.majorana-element")
    s16 = signed_sums(SIXTEEN)
    s15 = signed_sums(FIFTEEN)
    assert sum(SIXTEEN) == MODULUS and sum(FIFTEEN) == MODULUS - 1
    assert all(s % 2 == 1 for s in s15)                         # fifteen: every signed sum is odd
    assert sorted(set(s % MODULUS for s in s16 if s % MODULUS == 0)) == [0]
    zero16 = [s for s in s16 if s % MODULUS == 0]
    assert MODULUS in zero16 and -MODULUS in zero16 and 0 in zero16          # uniform, and balanced choices
    # three fifteen-component generations: no choice of signs gives a multiple of 16, or of 2
    vals15 = sorted(set(s15))
    for a in vals15:
        for b in vals15:
            for c in vals15:
                assert (a + b + c) % 2 == 1
    # two generations can cancel (opposite signs), so the obstruction is for odd numbers of generations
    assert any((a + b) % MODULUS == 0 for a in vals15 for b in vals15)
    # with the same uniform choice in each generation: 15 n_g = 0 mod 16 first at n_g = 16
    assert [g for g in range(1, MODULUS + 1) if (15 * g) % MODULUS == 0] == [MODULUS]
    return True
